Maybe you'll spend another 30 minutes answering follow-up questions. But once that knowledge is shared, the task is no longer solely yours to manage. You might even encourage them to share what they've learned with someone else in the team, spreading the knowledge even further. Over time, your team becomes capable of handling it independently. It might take a little effort up front, but soon enough, you'll no longer have to worry about it. The delivery risk will be removed and your team will be stronger for it.

想象一下，下周问题又出现了。你不再一个人冲上去，而是花 30 分钟和他们结对修复；或者更好——录一段操作讲解，或帮他们把流程记录下来。也许你还会再花 30 分钟回答后续问题。但一旦知识被分享出去，这个任务就不再只由你一人管理了。你甚至可以鼓励他们把学到的东西再分享给团队里的另一个人，让知识传播得更远。久而久之，你的团队就能独立处理它了。前期也许要花一点力气，但很快你就不必再为它操心。交付风险被消除，团队也因此更强。

Delegating tasks like this may take effort up front, but the long-term payoff is clear: your team becomes more capable, confident, and independent. You're

像这样授权任务，前期可能要花力气，但长期回报是明确的：你的团队变得更能干、更自信、更独立。你是在

— PDF p.179 —

investing in your team's resilience. Ultimately, that's the job of a great tech lead: scaling both your impact and the success of your team.

投资于团队的韧性。归根结底，这正是一位优秀技术负责人的工作：同时放大你自己的影响力和团队的成功。

Afraid of Losing the Credit害怕功劳被拿走

This fear is common but often unspoken. Many tech leads hesitate to delegate because they worry that if they're not the one directly producing the work, their contributions will go unnoticed. They fear that their impact will be invisible, that leadership or peers will recognize only the person who completed the task, not the one who made it happen.

这种恐惧很常见，却常常不曾说出口。许多技术负责人在授权时犹豫，因为他们担心：如果不是自己亲手产出工作，自己的贡献就会被忽视。他们担心自己的影响力会隐而不见，担心领导或同事只会认可那个完成任务的人，而不是那个让这件事得以发生的人。

I want to start by saying that this is a very normal fear and nothing to be ashamed of. The reason is simple: as individual contributors, tech leads were used to full ownership of their work, the outcomes, and all the praise that comes with it. This is how they've grown, how they've been evaluated, how they've built their careers. Promotions and recognition have always been tied to what they did, not necessarily what they enabled others to do. Shifting away from this mindset is complicated and takes time.

我想先说明：这是一种非常正常的恐惧，没什么可羞愧的。原因很简单：做个人贡献者时，技术负责人习惯了完全拥有自己的工作、成果，以及随之而来的所有赞誉。他们就是这样成长、这样被评估、这样建立起职业生涯的。晋升和认可，一向是和"他们自己做了什么"绑定在一起，而未必和"他们让别人做成了什么"挂钩。要从这种心态里转出来，既复杂又需要时间。

If this fear resonates with you, here's a story that might feel familiar. A tech lead I know was working on a critical performance optimization for their product. The issue had been on the radar for months, but due to other priorities, she hadn't been able to focus on it. When the time finally came to address it, she had a clear idea of how to tackle the problem but decided to delegate the task to a senior developer on the team so that it wouldn't be delayed any longer.

如果这种恐惧让你深有同感，下面这个故事你可能会觉得很熟悉。我认识的一位技术负责人，当时正在为自家产品做一项关键的性能优化。这个问题已经被关注好几个月了，但由于其他优先事项，她一直没能专注处理。当终于到了解决它的时候，她对如何着手已经有了清晰的思路，但为了不让它再拖延下去，她决定把任务授权给团队里的一位资深开发者。

She outlined the approach, provided guidance on what to look for, and even suggested a few potential solutions based on her prior research. She checked in regularly, helped troubleshoot blockers, and refined the approach when necessary but made a conscious effort to let the developer take ownership.

她勾勒了方法、给出了该关注什么的指导，甚至基于自己先前的研究提出了几个潜在方案。她定期跟进、帮忙排查阻塞、在必要时优化方法，但有意识地努力让这位开发者来当家作主。

A few weeks later, the developer successfully implemented the optimization, and the results were impressive: query response times improved by 40%, and system stability significantly improved. When the work was presented in a company-wide demo, leadership and peers applauded the developer for his great work. The team was also recognized for solving a long-standing problem, and the developer even got a personal shoutout from leadership in an all-hands meeting.

几周后，这位开发者成功实现了优化，结果令人印象深刻：查询响应时间提升了 40%，系统稳定性也显著改善。当这项工作在全公司的演示中展示时，领导和同事都为这位开发者出色的工作鼓掌。团队也因为解决了一个长期存在的问题而受到认可，这位开发者甚至在一次全员大会上被领导点名表扬。

The tech lead, however, received no direct recognition. The developer personally thanked her, but she would have liked others to know how she had guided, mentored, and provided solutions behind the scenes. While she was genuinely happy for the developer, she couldn't shake the feeling of being invisible in the process.

然而，这位技术负责人本人却没有得到任何直接的认可。那位开发者私下感谢了她，但她本希望其他人也能知道：在幕后，她是如何指导、带教并提供方案的。虽然她真心为这位开发者高兴，却挥之不去一种"在这个过程中隐身"的感觉。

— PDF p.180 —

This situation is exactly why many tech leads struggle with delegation. It's hard to let go when you fear that your impact will go unnoticed.

这种情形，正是许多技术负责人在授权时挣扎的原因。当你害怕自己的影响力会被忽视时，放手就变得很难。

But after some time, she started to see things differently. In her following one-on-ones with stakeholders and managers, she heard things like "That was a great achievement your team delivered. Sounds like you're doing a great job leading them and prioritizing tasks like this" or "I heard you had something to do with it."

但一段时间后，她开始换个角度看这件事。在接下来和干系人、经理的一对一里，她听到了这样的话："你的团队交付了一个了不起的成就。听起来你在带领他们、以及像这样排优先级方面做得很棒"，或者"我听说这件事里也有你的一份功劳"。

She realized that the credit did come back to her, just in a different way than she was used to. And when it came time for performance reviews, she wasn't writing, "I improved system performance by X%" but rather, "Led an initiative that improved system performance by X%." That subtle shift in framing made all the difference.

她意识到，功劳确实回到了她身上，只是方式和她过去习惯的不同。而到了绩效评估时，她写的不再是"我把系统性能提升了 X%"，而是"牵头了一项举措，把系统性能提升了 X%"。这种措辞上微妙的转变，带来了天壤之别。

As she continued to delegate more, leadership started recognizing her not just as an individual contributor but as someone who was building and enabling a strong, capable team. That's when it clicked: true leadership isn't about individual credit; it's about scaling impact. The fact that her team could execute at a high level without her needing to do everything herself was the real win.

随着她继续更多地授权，领导开始不再把她看作一个个人贡献者，而是看作一个正在建设并赋能一支强大、能干团队的人。那一刻她顿悟了：真正的领导力，不在于个人的功劳，而在于放大影响力。她的团队能够在不必事事由她亲为的情况下高水平执行，这才是真正的胜利。

As a tech lead, your success is no longer measured by the number of tasks you complete. Your value isn't tied to how much you deliver personally but how much your team delivers. That's what your stakeholders and leadership care about.

作为技术负责人，你的成功不再以你完成了多少任务来衡量。你的价值，不绑定于你个人交付了多少，而绑定于你的团队交付了多少。这才是你的干系人和领导真正关心的。

A big part of transitioning to leadership is understanding that it's not about you anymore. Your results are now your team's results. This shift requires moving from an I mindset to a We mindset:

向领导力转型很重要的一部分，就是明白：这不再是关于你自己了。你的成绩，现在就是你团队的成绩。这个转变，需要从"我"的心态走向"我们"的心态：

  • Instead of doing it yourself, empower your team to take ownership.与其自己动手，不如赋能团队去承担主人翁责任。
  • Instead of controlling every detail, focus on making your team more autonomous.与其控制每一个细节，不如专注于让团队更自主。
  • Instead of optimizing for the best short-term result, optimize for sustainable long-term growth.与其优化出最好的短期结果，不如优化出可持续的长期成长。
  • Instead of constantly checking up on or redoing your team's work, trust them and provide guidance when needed.与其不断查岗、或把团队的活儿重做一遍，不如信任他们，并在需要时提供指导。
  • And most importantly, instead of just taking accountability when things go wrong, share the credit when things go right.而最重要的是：与其只在出问题时承担责任，不如在事情顺利时把功劳分享出去。
— PDF p.181 —

In the situation mentioned earlier, the tech lead was very involved in the success of that performance optimization. But the best part is that, as a tech lead, you also get credit for things you weren't even directly involved in. Anything your team delivers is a reflection on you. Whether you were closely involved in the task or not, you will always be associated with the results of your team. The credit might not be instant or as direct as when you were an individual contributor, but it's there. And more importantly, the impact of your work is multiplied by the people you lead.

在前面提到的那个情形里，这位技术负责人深度参与了那次性能优化的成功。但最妙的是：作为技术负责人，即便有些事你并没有直接参与，功劳也会落到你头上。团队交付的任何成果，都是你的一面镜子。无论你是否深度介入那个任务，你永远都会和团队的结果联系在一起。这份功劳，也许不会像你做个人贡献者时那样立竿见影、那样直接，但它确实在那里。而更重要的是：你工作的影响力，会被你所领导的人成倍放大。

Key Takeaway本章要点

Stepping into a tech lead role means redefining how you create impact. Your value isn't tied to doing everything yourself; it comes from how well you guide and support your team to succeed.

走上技术负责人这个岗位，意味着重新定义你创造影响力的方式。你的价值，不绑定于事事亲为；它来自你引导和支持团队走向成功的本领有多高。

Delegation plays a central role in that shift. When you delegate effectively, you create space for your team to grow, take ownership, and develop confidence. At the same time, you gain the bandwidth to focus on higher-level priorities like team alignment, system design, and long-term strategy.

授权在这个转变中扮演着核心角色。当你高效授权时，你为团队创造了成长、承担主人翁责任和建立自信的空间。与此同时，你也获得了带宽，去专注于更高层次的优先事项，比如团队对齐、系统设计和长期战略。

This shift can feel uncomfortable. It takes time to build trust in others and in your own ability to lead without micromanaging. You may feel the urge to stay involved in every detail, especially if you're used to being the go-to person for execution.

这个转变一开始可能会让人不适。要建立起对他人的信任、以及对自己"在不微观管理的情况下带领团队"的信心，需要时间。你可能会忍不住想介入每一个细节，尤其是如果你早已习惯做那个执行上事事找的人。

But strong leadership means creating an environment where great work happens through others. When you invest in delegation, you're investing in your team's strength and in your own evolution as a leader. That's what unlocks real, sustainable impact.

但强有力的领导力，意味着创造一个"通过他人成就卓越工作"的环境。当你投资于授权时，你既是在投资于团队的实力，也是在投资于你自己作为领导者的进化。而这，才是解锁真正、可持续影响力的关键。
